We have template 1914386. Need to propose retrosynthesis route for target SMILES: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O.

We need to apply this template in retrosynthetic direction (i.e., break target into precursors). The template's retro_smarts: '[C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D3;+0:13]1=[CH;D2;+0:14]-[C;H0;D4;+0:1]-1(/[CH;D2;+0:2]=[CH;D2;+0:3]/[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8]>>O=[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[c:4])-[C:5](=[O;D1;H0:6])-[#8:7]-[C;D1;H3:8].[C;D1;H3:9]-[#14:10](-[C;D1;H3:11])(-[C;D1;H3:12])-[C;H0;D2;+0:13]#[CH;D1;+0:14]'

So forward reaction (template) takes two fragments: a silyl alkyne? Actually product side is two fragments: an ester (O=C... ) and a silyl alkyne? Wait.

Retro direction: target (product) is the left side of ">>"? Actually retro_smarts: left side is reactants? In retrosynthesis, we apply template to target to get precursors (reactants). The template's retro_smarts shows mapping from product to reactants? Usually retro_smarts is pattern for product, and right side are precursors. In the JSON, they gave retro_smarts: left side is product pattern, right side is precursors. So applying retrosynthesis to target will match left side and produce right side fragments.

Thus we need to see if our target matches left side pattern. Let's attempt to apply template to target using apply_template tool.
